headline: What’s in
the shot.
dek: B12, lipo and MIC injections are sold for energy. The trials are few, or none.
byline: Adonis Men’s Health · Checked Oct 31, 2026 · Clinical review pending

glance.label: B12 for energy
glance.line: Two small placebo-controlled trials. Neither found a difference from placebo.

glance.label: MIC blends
glance.line: Compounded, not FDA approved. No published human study of injected M, I or C for energy.

glance.label: Semax
glance.line: Registered in Russia, as nasal drops. HHS compounding discretion in the US since Oct 30, 2026.

summary: Injections sold for energy are built around [[/vitamin-b12|vitamin B12]], often in “MIC” lipotropic blends named for the [[/methionine|methionine]], [[/inositol|inositol]] and [[/choline|choline]] they contain, sometimes with [[/vitamin-b6|vitamin B6]] or [[/l-carnitine|L-carnitine]]. These blends are compounded and not FDA approved. FDA’s recall records list many compounded lipotropic and MIC injections recalled by pharmacies, most often for lack of assurance of sterility.

B12 itself is approved for one job: cyanocobalamin injection treats B12 deficiency caused by poor absorption. Injecting it for energy in someone who is not deficient is off-label. In the two small placebo-controlled trials we found, 20 singers and 15 people with chronic fatigue syndrome did about as well on placebo as on the B12 injection. B6 and L-carnitine injections are approved for deficiency, not energy, and we found no published human study of injected methionine, inositol or choline for energy or fat loss.

[[/semax|Semax]], a synthetic fragment of the hormone ACTH, is the lane’s one peptide. FDA’s 2026 review found it registered as a medicine in Russia, as nasal drops. Its human studies are small, almost all Russian, and all used nasal drops. It is not FDA approved; since October 30, 2026, HHS has allowed it to be compounded for use in the nose under set conditions, which is enforcement discretion, not approval. WADA’s list does not name it.

What is not known: whether B12 shots help energy in people with normal B12, what the MIC blends do at all, and whether Semax is safe or effective outside the Russian studies. FDA found no study of Semax given by injection.

pull.quote: Semax is a registered drug in Russia and is available as 0.1% and 1% nasal drops.

excerpts.quote: Cyanocobalamin is indicated for vitamin B 12 deficiencies due to malabsorption which may be associated with the following conditions: Addisonian (pernicious) anemia
excerpts.note: The label goes on to list other causes of poor absorption. Energy is not among the approved uses.

excerpts.quote: The parenteral route is indicated when oral administration is not feasible as in anorexia, nausea and vomiting, and preoperative and postoperative conditions.
excerpts.note: The approved B6 injection is for deficiency when B6 cannot be taken by mouth.

excerpts.quote: No studies were found in which semax was used as a compounded drug product.
excerpts.source: FDA briefing on Semax, Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee
excerpts.note: This is FDA’s own briefing to its advisers.

excerpts.quote: At the time of this evaluation, the nominator did not submit, and FDA did not identify nonclinical developmental and reproductive studies of semax.
excerpts.source: FDA briefing on Semax, Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee

excerpts.quote: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial found that after empirical vitamin B12 injection to improve mild voice-related symptoms, the improvement in self-reported voice measures in singers shows no meaningful difference compared with placebo.
excerpts.source: Shoffel-Havakuk et al., JAMA Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg

excerpts.quote: Although patients responded to placebo and LEFAC by several criteria of functional status, no significant difference was apparent between response to placebo and that to LEFAC. The placebo response appeared to be strong.
excerpts.source: Kaslow et al., Arch Intern Med
excerpts.note: LEFAC was an injection of liver extract, folic acid and B12, given to 15 people with chronic fatigue syndrome.

excerpts.quote: On Friday afternoon, the committee voted 8-5-1 for semax in both acetate and free-base forms. Most of the ‘no’ voters cited safety concerns.
excerpts.source: Healio, “FDA committee recommends looser restrictions for several peptides”
excerpts.note: FDA has not posted the official vote record.
